Hey Voat!

I am hoping some of you here have experience with driving through the night and could offer me some tips or advice.

I will be driving tomorrow night from 8PM till at least 3AM. Unfortunately this is my only option. I'm a bit nervous, never having done a drive like this. Can I just keep myself going on red bull and nicotine to power through it?

Thanks in advance my beloved goats
Advice for late night road trip?
If you can, sleep the night before and nap during the day when you can. Red bull and nicotine will help, between the sleeping and the stimulants you can do it!
Make sure to take some breaks to get out of the car every 2 hours and walk around for 10 minutes. It seems like a waste of time, but helped me a lot on overnight trips.
Get some of your favorite snacks and some good music should help.

Hey there, friend. Longtime night owl. Be mindful of that pesky circadian rhythm!

Audiobook and/or Podcasts are great; they tend to stimulate your mind more than music. Don't rely solely on caffeine to keep yourself awake unless you're very sensitive to it and know it'll keep you up.

Also. Get a restful nap beforehand. Try Sleepyti.me as a calculator for help — that site is great on its own, regardless.

Good luck and stay safe.

I have frequently done this. My best recommendation, take a break from driving every 3 hours or so. If you are into podcasts get a few extras, look for some comedians or topics that you find incredibly interesting. If not that, music. Nothing soft. It needs to be something you feel like grooving to. Roll down your window. You don't want to get too warm or comfortable.

Above all else, if you feel tired at all, pull the fuck over. Don't feel like you have to power through it. Nothing is so important that you should risk the lives of other people on the road.

We take most of our road trips at night. It is cooler and less traffic, except for the semi trucks of course. My suggestions are take someone with you, this will help keep you awake. Satellite radio. I love mine and listen to comedy when I get sleepy. Snacks and drinks. I stay away from coffee or energy drinks until I absolutely need them, it helps to wake you up more then. As the other user noted, get out and walk and use the bathroom frequently. You will be surprised how much this will wake you up. And last thing make sure your car maintenance is up to spec. Last thing you want us to break down in the middle of the night. Earlier this year we drove from 6 pm to 9 am in a snow storm from S.C. to Virginia. Had no issues at all and stopped for extended periods of time to get a snack and change of scenery.

I've done a lot of distance driving and most of all, unless you've got to be somewhere at 3AM (which sounds a lot more interesting than my life), give yourself permission to pull over and take a nap. If you do this, text whoever's expecting you so that they don't freak out when you're late. You'll feel a bit grimy but it's better than waking up wrapped up in someone else's front bumper.
I've done a drive like this. Put your windows down and AC on full blast when you start feeling sleepy. I don't care how cold you are, keep it on.
Depending on where you are, do not blow off those watch for elk signs! Last time i went through mountains after midnight 3 of them jumped out, but luckily I was going slow enough to avoid them.

Something that keeps your mind going. If you have people with you make sure they are awake and keep you awake. If you're alone then music, coffee, chew gum, talk to yourself. Anything that keeps your mind active.

I drove up to NY from FL a few years ago with my GF at the time and her 2 cousins. Going through both Carolinas in the middle of the night - everyone else was sleeping - all I had to keep me awake was a single earbud plugged into my phone with some music. It was painful. If you've never driven through the Carolinas, it's just like 7 hours of straight roads and nothing but trees. All you're doing is staring at trees passing you the entire time, but you can't fall asleep, and it was pitch black and I was tired. It's torture.

This is a followup to this post: https://www.voat.co/v/ideasforvoat/comments/133388

I said I would look at the source code, so I did some poking around and from what I see the only time a post gets its rank assigned is when it is voted on. I tested this hypothesis by going to an under-used sub (/v/cars was my test case) and looking for a submission on the front page that was aged 3 months. I voated on the post and it dropped off the front page. I found the post and removed my voat, just to check, and the post remained off the front page.

Additionally, it looks like submissions never have their rank set when they are initially created. This is why the front page occasionally gets flooded with massive amounts of posts that are 1-5 minutes old. To test this post I went to the first page and voated on some submissions that were < 5 minutes old with 2 or 3 points. Even when I upvoated these posts, they immediately dropped off the front page on a page refresh.
Ok, so I think I've figured out why the front page gets flooded with posts that are only 1-5 minutes old

Just confirmed this — I bumped about a couple hundred of 2-5 point submissions off of /v/all's Hot queue and it is now filled with double-/triple-digit submissions. For anyone interested in "community service", just upvoat everything on the front page and remove your upvoats afterward.
Did the same to test it out and it works, but /v/all is just filled with new 2-5 point submissions right after this.

It looks like the current ranking formula is

rank = max(score - 1, 0)0.8 / (hours_old + 2)1.8

The big problem with using the age of the post this way is that the age of a post is constantly increasing, so the ranks of posts would have to constantly be updated to correctly take the passage of time into account (otherwise, you get the current situation where posts are "stuck" with a high rank because nobody's voted on them for a while, and then upvoting them knocks them down). As the number of posts grows over time, keeping them all reasonably up to date would put more and more load on the database.

The solution is to make the ranking formula into an "adjusted timestamp" that does not depend on the current time - basically, it should be of the form

rank = time_posted + (some formula only involving score)
I really like the idea of the adjusted time stamp.

The formula is taken from Hacker News, so I doubt Atko will change it. The problem is with re-ranking process, maybe submissions should be re-ranked when the page is shown to the user or something (50 exponentiations per user view in worst case, is that a huge number?)

I also think the score part can be pre-calculated up to 1000 and stored in a table, maybe that will be faster.
